import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", rc={"axes.facecolor": (0, 0, 0, 0)})

# Create a FacetGrid to plot survival rate across different attributes
g = sns.FacetGrid(df, row="sex", col="pclass", hue="survived", height=3.5, aspect=1.2,
                  palette={0: '#D55E00', 1: '#0072B2'}, margin_titles=True)

# Plot the density of age for survivors and non-survivors
g.map(sns.kdeplot, "age", fill=True, alpha=0.7, lw=2)

# Add a horizontal line for each subplot
g.map(plt.axhline, y=0, lw=2, clip_on=False, color='black')

# Function to add labels to each subplot
def label(x, color, label):
    ax = plt.gca()
    ax.text(0.05, 0.85, label, fontweight="bold", color=color,
            ha="left", va="center", transform=ax.transAxes)

g.map(label, "age")

# Adjust the subplots to overlap slightly
g.fig.subplots_adjust(hspace=-.5)

# Remove axes details that don't play well with overlap
g.set_titles("")
g.set(yticks=[], ylabel="")
g.despine(bottom=True, left=True)

# Add a clear, informative title
g.fig.suptitle('Age Distribution of Titanic Passengers by Survival, Class, and Sex',
               y=1.05, fontsize=18, fontweight='bold')
plt.figtext(0.5, 0.98, 'Density plot showing a higher survival rate for women and children, especially in higher classes',
            ha='center', fontsize=12, style='italic')

# Create a custom legend
survived_patch = mpatches.Patch(color='#0072B2', label='Survived')
not_survived_patch = mpatches.Patch(color='#D55E00', label='Did Not Survive')
plt.legend(handles=[survived_patch, not_survived_patch],
           title='Status', bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 3.5), loc='upper right')

# Set axis labels for the bottom-left plot for context
g.axes[1,0].set_xlabel('Age', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
g.axes[0,0].set_ylabel('Female', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
g.axes[1,0].set_ylabel('Male', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Set column titles
g.axes[0,0].set_title('First Class', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
g.axes[0,1].set_title('Second Class', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
g.axes[0,2].set_title('Third Class', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
